limits: Chapter states it is not a data engineering book and keeps it to what is strictly necessary.
Scale is hundreds of documents; no throughput, cost or quality measurements.
Crawler code is shown with truncated lines in the web copy.
Medium/LinkedIn crawlers depend on Selenium login and ChromeDriver, which the chapter calls a well-known source of problems; no mention of platform terms of service.
Cleaning/normalization is minimal (html2text, soup.get_text()); further cleaning deferred to the feature pipeline in ch. 4.
practices: Collect your own data to mimic real-world projects rather than using a static dataset (intro).
Normalize by data category (article, repository, post), not by source; keep the source URL in metadata (Designing, p.3-4).
Use a dispatcher over a common BaseCrawler interface with a fallback crawler (p.8-10).
Check for an existing record by link before crawling to avoid duplicates (crawler extract methods).
Structure data in Pydantic classes, not dicts, for type validation (NoSQL documents, p.18).
Use an ODM base class to share CRUD code across document classes (p.19-22).
Use a schemaless NoSQL store for unstructured text at small scale; use Snowflake/BigQuery at millions of documents (p.4-5).
Record per-domain successful/total crawl counts as pipeline artifact metadata for monitoring (p.7, 26).
Ship a backup of the raw data so later chapters run if crawlers fail (Troubleshooting, p.28).

terms.definition: Extract data from sources, transform it by cleaning and standardizing, load it into a data warehouse or database.
Object-Document Mapping: like ORM but for NoSQL databases; maps object-oriented code to JSON-like documents.
A technique that lets you query and manipulate data from a database using an object-oriented paradigm.
